problem.title: Chickens and Rabbits
problem.statement: A pen holds 12 animals, all chickens or rabbits. Altogether they have 34 legs. How many rabbits are in the pen?
hints: Compare with the leg total if all twelve animals were chickens.

solutionSteps.title: Write both constraints
solutionSteps.body: The system is c + r = 12 and 2c + 4r = 34.

solutionSteps.title: Eliminate and check
solutionSteps.body: Double the first equation and subtract to get 2r = 10, so r = 5 and c = 7. Then 7 + 5 = 12 and 2(7) + 4(5) = 34.

validationMethods: elimination: subtract 2c + 2r = 24 from 2c + 4r = 34 to obtain r = 5
independent baseline count: twelve chickens give 24 legs and each rabbit replacement adds 2, so the 10-leg gap requires 5 rabbits; all options audited
notes: The animal context differs from both mapped bank problems and uses only prerequisite linear-equation skills.

problem.title: Dimes and Quarters
problem.statement: A jar contains 14 coins, all dimes or quarters, worth 245 cents altogether. How many quarters are in the jar?
hints: Compare the value with fourteen dimes.

solutionSteps.title: Align and subtract
solutionSteps.body: Multiply d + q = 14 by 10, then subtract it from 10d + 25q = 245. This gives 15q = 105, so q = 7.

solutionSteps.title: Check
solutionSteps.body: Seven quarters and seven dimes make 14 coins worth 175 + 70 = 245 cents.

validationMethods: independent substitution and exhaustive choice audit: only 7 quarters with 7 dimes totals 14 coins and 245 cents

problem.title: Two Ticket Prices
problem.statement: A theater sold 20 tickets. Adult tickets cost 8 dollars and child tickets cost 5 dollars. The total revenue was 127 dollars. How many adult tickets were sold?
hints: Scale the complete count equation by five.

solutionSteps.title: Eliminate
solutionSteps.body: Multiply a + c = 20 by 5 to obtain 5a + 5c = 100. Subtract from 8a + 5c = 127 to get 3a = 27, so a = 9.

validationMethods: equation elimination: revenue minus five times ticket count gives 3a = 27, hence a = 9
independent baseline audit: twenty child tickets earn 100 dollars; each adult replacement adds 3 dollars, so a 27-dollar gap needs 9 replacements; all choices evaluated

problem.title: A Sum and a Difference
problem.statement: Two numbers x and y satisfy x + y = 23 and x - y = 7. What is x?
hints: Add corresponding sides of the two equations.
The y and -y terms will cancel.

solutionSteps.title: Add equations
solutionSteps.body: Adding x + y = 23 and x - y = 7 gives 2x = 30, so x = 15.

solutionSteps.title: Check the pair
solutionSteps.body: Then y = 8. The pair satisfies 15 + 8 = 23 and 15 - 8 = 7.

validationMethods: direct addition of the equations gives 2x = 30 and x = 15
independent reconstruction: half of the sum-plus-difference is (23 + 7) / 2 = 15; exhaustive option substitution confirms uniqueness

problem.title: Rectangle from Two Clues
problem.statement: A rectangle has perimeter 34 units. Its length is 5 units greater than its width. What is its area in square units?
hints: Use l + w = 17 and l - w = 5.
Find both dimensions before calculating area.

solutionSteps.title: Translate and solve
solutionSteps.body: The perimeter gives l + w = 17, and the difference gives l - w = 5. Adding yields 2l = 22, so l = 11 and w = 6.

solutionSteps.title: Check and answer
solutionSteps.body: The perimeter is 2(11) + 2(6) = 34 and the difference is 5. The area is 11 × 6 = 66 square units.

validationMethods: system solution: l + w = 17 and l - w = 5 give l = 11, w = 6, area 66
independent factor-pair audit: among positive factor pairs for each offered area, only 11 by 6 has perimeter 34 and side difference 5
